category: Core verbs: the body and health

entries.meaning: To take air into your lungs and let it out again. ---
examples: Breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth.
She breathed a little easier once the fever broke.
He was breathing hard by the time he reached the top floor.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (breathe clean air), intransitive (she breathed slowly)
entries.contrast: The noun is breath /brɛθ/, short vowel and voiceless th; the verb breathe /briːð/ has a long vowel and a voiced th. You take a breath, then you breathe.

entries.meaning: To let air out of your lungs. ---
examples: Exhale slowly as you lower the weight.
She exhaled and finally let her shoulders drop.
The nurse asked him to keep exhaling into the tube.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (exhale the smoke), intransitive (exhale slowly)

entries.meaning: To push air out of your throat with a sudden loud noise, usually because you are sick. ---
examples: He coughs all night when his allergies flare up.
She coughed so hard her chest hurt.
The baby has been coughing since Tuesday.
entries.contrast: The gh is said as /f/: cough rhymes with off, not with though.

entries.meaning: To suddenly blow air out through your nose and mouth in a way you cannot control. ---
examples: Pepper always makes me sneeze.
She sneezed three times in a row.
He kept sneezing all through the meeting.

entries.meaning: To open your mouth wide and breathe in deeply because you are tired or bored. ---
examples: Try not to yawn while she is explaining it.
He yawned and looked at the clock.
Half the class was yawning by ten after eight.

entries.meaning: To breathe in suddenly and loudly, from shock or from a lack of air. ---
examples: The cold water made her gasp.
He gasped when he saw the hospital bill.
She came up out of the pool gasping for air.

entries.meaning: To breathe in quick short breaths after hard exercise or in heat. ---
examples: The dog starts to pant the second we go outside.
She panted up the last flight of stairs.
He was panting too hard to answer me.

entries.meaning: To breathe with a rough whistling sound, usually because of asthma or a chest infection. ---
examples: He tends to wheeze in cold air.
She wheezed through the whole night.
The doctor listened to his chest while he was wheezing.

entries.meaning: To breathe with a loud rough noise while you are asleep. ---
examples: My husband snores every single night.
He snored through the entire movie.
I couldn't sleep with someone snoring next to me.

entries.meaning: To die or almost die because you cannot get any air. ---
examples: A plastic bag can suffocate a small child.
Two people suffocated in the smoke before the crew arrived.
The heat in that attic is suffocating.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the smoke suffocated them), intransitive (he nearly suffocated)

entries.meaning: To sleep for a short time during the day. ---
examples: I nap for twenty minutes after lunch.
The baby napped in the car the whole way home.
He was napping on the couch when we got in.
entries.contrast: One syllable, one vowel, one final consonant — so the p doubles: napped, napping.

entries.meaning: To sleep lightly, often without meaning to. ---
examples: Grandpa likes to doze in his chair after dinner.
She dozed through most of the flight.
He was dozing with the TV still on.

entries.meaning: To sleep lightly for a short while, or to push the alarm back for a few more minutes. ---
examples: I always snooze the alarm twice.
He snoozed on the train and missed his stop.
She was snoozing in the sun on the back steps.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (snooze the alarm), intransitive (snooze for an hour)

entries.meaning: To become tired, or to make someone tired. ---
examples: Stairs tire him more than they used to.
She tired quickly in the weeks after surgery.
The heat was tiring the runners before the halfway mark.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the climb tired us), intransitive (he tires easily)

entries.meaning: To get your strength and health back after an illness or a hard effort. ---
examples: It takes a week to recuperate from that kind of flu.
He recuperated at his sister's place for a month.
She is still recuperating from the operation.

entries.meaning: Exercise has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Try to exercise three times a week.
He exercised every morning for a year.
She has been exercising since her doctor warned her.
Please exercise caution on the icy steps.
She exercised her right to remain silent.
The governor has rarely exercised the veto.

senses.head: To move your body in order to stay fit and healthy
examples: Try to exercise three times a week.
He exercised every morning for a year.
She has been exercising since her doctor warned her.

senses.head: To use a right, a power, or a quality that you have
examples: Please exercise caution on the icy steps.
She exercised her right to remain silent.
The governor has rarely exercised the veto.

entries.русский: заниматься спортом, тренироваться; осуществлять, использовать (право); проявлять (осторожность)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (exercise the dog), intransitive (exercise every morning)

entries.meaning: To bend a joint or tighten a muscle. ---
examples: Flex your foot toward your knee and hold it.
He flexed his arm to show me the bruise.
The therapist watched her flexing her fingers.

entries.meaning: Squat has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Squat down and lift with your legs.
He squatted beside the bed to talk to her.
She was squatting to pick up the baby when her back gave out.
Several families squat in the old hotel.
He squatted in an empty warehouse for two years.
People have been squatting in the building since it closed.

senses.head: To lower your body by bending your knees while keeping your back straight
examples: Squat down and lift with your legs.
He squatted beside the bed to talk to her.
She was squatting to pick up the baby when her back gave out.

senses.head: To live in an empty building without permission and without paying rent
examples: Several families squat in the old hotel.
He squatted in an empty warehouse for two years.
People have been squatting in the building since it closed.

entries.русский: приседать, присесть; самовольно занимать (пустующее жильё), сквоттерствовать

entries.meaning: Stagger has 3 distinct senses.
examples: People stagger a little when their blood pressure drops.
He staggered to the couch and sat down.
She was staggering by the end of the shift.
The repair bill will stagger you.
The size of the crowd staggered the organizers.
I was staggered by how much the house sold for.
The school will stagger start times by half an hour.
They staggered the shifts to keep the floor from getting crowded.
Boarding is staggered by row.

senses.head: To walk unsteadily, as though you are about to fall
examples: People stagger a little when their blood pressure drops.
He staggered to the couch and sat down.
She was staggering by the end of the shift.

senses.head: To shock or amaze someone
examples: The repair bill will stagger you.
The size of the crowd staggered the organizers.
I was staggered by how much the house sold for.

senses.head: To arrange times so that they do not all happen at once
examples: The school will stagger start times by half an hour.
They staggered the shifts to keep the floor from getting crowded.
Boarding is staggered by row.

entries.русский: шататься, пошатнуться; потрясать, потрясти; поражать, ошеломлять; разносить по времени, распределять (смены, время начала)
entries.contrast: Stress falls on the first syllable, so the r does not double: staggered, staggering.

entries.meaning: To move your head down and up to say yes or to greet someone. ---
examples: Just nod if you understand what I'm asking.
She nodded and took the prescription.
He was nodding along to everything the doctor said.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (nod your head), intransitive (he nodded politely)

entries.meaning: To raise your shoulders to show that you do not know or do not care. ---
examples: Don't just shrug — tell me where it hurts.
He shrugged and looked at the floor.
She answered by shrugging her shoulders.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (shrug your shoulders), intransitive (he just shrugged)

entries.meaning: To make a sudden face because of pain. ---
examples: Tell me where you wince when I press.
She winced as the doctor touched the bruise.
He was wincing with every step.

entries.meaning: To move back suddenly because you are afraid of being hurt. ---
examples: Most kids flinch when they see the needle.
She flinched away from the bright light.
He took the shot without flinching.

entries.meaning: To make a long low sound of pain or complaint. ---
examples: Patients often moan as the anesthetic wears off.
He moaned softly and asked for water.
She was moaning about her back all afternoon.

entries.meaning: To hurt in a steady beating rhythm. ---
examples: My finger throbs every time I lower my hand.
His tooth throbbed all night.
She woke up with a throbbing headache.

entries.meaning: To lose consciousness for a short time. ---
examples: Some people faint at the sight of blood.
She fainted in the shower and cut her forehead.
He has fainted twice this month.

entries.meaning: Relapse has 2 distinct senses.
examples: About a third of patients relapse within a year.
He relapsed two months after the treatment ended.
She is terrified of relapsing again.
Most people relapse at least once.
He relapsed after eight months sober.
She has relapsed twice since the program ended.

senses.head: To become ill again after you seemed to be getting better
examples: About a third of patients relapse within a year.
He relapsed two months after the treatment ended.
She is terrified of relapsing again.

senses.head: To start drinking, using drugs, or repeating a bad habit again after stopping
examples: Most people relapse at least once.
He relapsed after eight months sober.
She has relapsed twice since the program ended.

entries.русский: снова заболеть, дать рецидив; срываться, сорваться; возвращаться к прежней привычке
entries.contrast: The verb stresses the second syllable, ri-LAPS; the noun a relapse is often REE-laps.

entries.meaning: Survive has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Most people survive this kind of surgery without trouble.
He survived the crash with a broken arm.
She has survived two rounds of chemotherapy.
She is survived by two sons and a sister.
He survived his wife by ten years.
Nobody expected the youngest brother to survive them all.

senses.head: To stay alive through an illness, an accident, or a dangerous situation
examples: Most people survive this kind of surgery without trouble.
He survived the crash with a broken arm.
She has survived two rounds of chemotherapy.

senses.head: To remain alive after another person has died
body: (пережить (кого-либо), остаться в живых после чьей-то смерти)
examples: She is survived by two sons and a sister.
He survived his wife by ten years.
Nobody expected the youngest brother to survive them all.

entries.русский: выживать, выжить; пережить (кого-либо), остаться в живых после чьей-то смерти
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (survive the surgery), intransitive (only two survived)

entries.meaning: To produce sweat, especially when you are hot or nervous. ---
examples: Athletes perspire much more in humid weather.
He perspired through his shirt during the exam.
She was perspiring heavily and looked pale.

entries.meaning: Contract has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Workers can contract the virus from contaminated water.
He contracted pneumonia in the hospital.
She had contracted the infection weeks before any symptoms showed.
Metal contracts as it cools.
The muscle contracted sharply and he dropped the bar.
Her pupils were contracting in the bright light.

senses.head: To catch a serious illness
examples: Workers can contract the virus from contaminated water.
He contracted pneumonia in the hospital.
She had contracted the infection weeks before any symptoms showed.

senses.head: To become smaller or shorter, or to make something do this
examples: Metal contracts as it cools.
The muscle contracted sharply and he dropped the bar.
Her pupils were contracting in the bright light.

entries.русский: заразиться, подхватить (болезнь); сжиматься, сокращаться; сжимать, сократить
entries.contrast: As a verb the stress is on the second syllable, kuhn-TRAKT. The noun a contract (a legal agreement) is KAHN-trakt.

entries.meaning: To keep a person or animal away from others so a disease cannot spread. ---
examples: The shelter quarantines every new dog for ten days.
He was quarantined for two weeks after the trip.
The hospital is quarantining the whole floor.

entries.meaning: To make your skin darker by staying in the sun. ---
examples: Some people burn, others just tan.
She tanned easily even as a kid.
He spent the week tanning on the beach and paid for it later.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the sun tanned his arms), intransitive (she tans easily)

entries.meaning: To push a bone out of its normal place at a joint. ---
examples: Throwing that hard can dislocate a shoulder.
He dislocated his finger catching the ball.
She has dislocated the same shoulder twice.

entries.meaning: Scar has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Deep cuts almost always scar.
The burn scarred his forearm.
Her knee is badly scarred from the surgery.
Losing a parent young can scar a child for life.
The divorce scarred both of them.
He came home scarred by what he had seen overseas.

senses.head: To leave a permanent mark on the skin after a wound heals
examples: Deep cuts almost always scar.
The burn scarred his forearm.
Her knee is badly scarred from the surgery.

senses.head: To harm someone emotionally in a way that lasts for years
examples: Losing a parent young can scar a child for life.
The divorce scarred both of them.
He came home scarred by what he had seen overseas.

entries.русский: оставлять шрам, покрываться шрамами; травмировать, оставлять глубокий след (в душе)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the burn scarred his arm), intransitive (deep cuts scar)
entries.contrast: The r doubles: scarred, scarring — one r would give scared (frightened), a different word.

entries.meaning: To identify what illness someone has. ---
examples: It can take years to diagnose this condition.
They diagnosed her with diabetes at thirty.
He was diagnosed last spring.
entries.contrast: You diagnose a person with a disease, or diagnose the disease itself — never 'diagnose a person of'.

entries.meaning: Prescribe has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Doctors rarely prescribe antibiotics for a cold.
She prescribed something for the pain.
He has been prescribed two different inhalers.
The law prescribes a minimum sentence of five years.
The manual prescribed exactly how the tanks were to be cleaned.
Meetings must be held at the times prescribed in the bylaws.

senses.head: To officially tell a patient to take a certain medicine or treatment
examples: Doctors rarely prescribe antibiotics for a cold.
She prescribed something for the pain.
He has been prescribed two different inhalers.

senses.head: To state officially what must be done or how it must be done
examples: The law prescribes a minimum sentence of five years.
The manual prescribed exactly how the tanks were to be cleaned.
Meetings must be held at the times prescribed in the bylaws.

entries.русский: прописывать, выписывать (лекарство); предписывать, предписать; устанавливать (правила, порядок)

entries.meaning: Inject has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Diabetics inject insulin every day.
The nurse injected the dye before the scan.
He was injecting himself in the stomach.
She injected some humor into a very dull meeting.
The loan injected cash into the business at the right moment.
The new coach is injecting energy into the team.

senses.head: To put medicine into the body with a needle
examples: Diabetics inject insulin every day.
The nurse injected the dye before the scan.
He was injecting himself in the stomach.

senses.head: To add a new quality or element to something
examples: She injected some humor into a very dull meeting.
The loan injected cash into the business at the right moment.
The new coach is injecting energy into the team.

entries.русский: вводить инъекцию, делать укол; привносить, привнести; вливать (средства, энергию)

entries.meaning: To give someone a vaccine to protect them from a disease. ---
examples: Clinics vaccinate children against measles.
She vaccinated both kids last fall.
He has been vaccinated twice this year.
entries.contrast: Two cs: vaccinate. You vaccinate someone against a disease.

entries.meaning: To clean something with a substance that kills germs. ---
examples: Disinfect the cut before you cover it.
She disinfected the counter after handling the chicken.
The room is disinfected between patients.

entries.meaning: Sterilize has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Boil the bottles to sterilize them.
The nurse sterilized the instruments.
Everything on that tray has been sterilized.
The shelter will sterilize every animal before adoption.
The vet sterilized our cat last spring.
All the dogs here have been sterilized.

senses.head: To make equipment completely free of germs, usually with heat or chemicals
examples: Boil the bottles to sterilize them.
The nurse sterilized the instruments.
Everything on that tray has been sterilized.

senses.head: To operate on a person or an animal so that they cannot have young
examples: The shelter will sterilize every animal before adoption.
The vet sterilized our cat last spring.
All the dogs here have been sterilized.

entries.русский: стерилизовать, обеззараживать; стерилизовать (лишать способности иметь потомство)
entries.contrast: American English spells it -ize: sterilize, sterilized. British English also allows sterilise.

entries.meaning: Nurse has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Somebody has to nurse him through this.
She nursed her mother for two years.
He is at home nursing a broken rib.
The puppies nurse every couple of hours.
She nursed both of her children for a year.
He fell asleep while nursing.
She still nurses a quiet hope of moving back.
He nursed a grudge against his brother for years.
They have been nursing that grievance since the merger.

senses.head: To take care of someone who is sick or injured
examples: Somebody has to nurse him through this.
She nursed her mother for two years.
He is at home nursing a broken rib.

senses.head: To feed a baby milk from the breast
examples: The puppies nurse every couple of hours.
She nursed both of her children for a year.
He fell asleep while nursing.

senses.head: To hold on to a feeling for a long time
examples: She still nurses a quiet hope of moving back.
He nursed a grudge against his brother for years.
They have been nursing that grievance since the merger.

entries.русский: ухаживать за больным, выхаживать; кормить грудью; сосать грудь (о младенце); лелеять, вынашивать (чувство); затаить (обиду)

entries.meaning: To put someone in a hospital for treatment. ---
examples: They only hospitalize the worst cases.
He was hospitalized for a week with pneumonia.
Hundreds have been hospitalized this flu season.

entries.meaning: Transplant has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Surgeons can now transplant a whole face.
They transplanted a kidney from his brother.
Her cornea was transplanted last year.
Wait until fall to transplant the roses.
We transplanted the seedlings into bigger pots.
The tomatoes are ready to be transplanted outside.

senses.head: To move an organ or piece of tissue from one body into another
examples: Surgeons can now transplant a whole face.
They transplanted a kidney from his brother.
Her cornea was transplanted last year.

senses.head: To dig up a plant and put it in the ground somewhere else
examples: Wait until fall to transplant the roses.
We transplanted the seedlings into bigger pots.
The tomatoes are ready to be transplanted outside.

entries.contrast: The verb stresses the second syllable, trans-PLANT; the noun a transplant stresses the first, TRANS-plant.

entries.meaning: Discharge has 4 distinct senses.
examples: They usually discharge you the next morning.
She was discharged after two nights.
He is being discharged this afternoon.
He was discharged from the Army after four years.
A company may discharge an employee for theft.
Having been dishonorably discharged, he had trouble finding work.
The plant discharges wastewater into the river.
The factory discharged chemicals for years before anyone noticed.
Pipes along the roof were discharging steam into the cold air.
It is illegal to discharge a firearm inside city limits.
The officer discharged his weapon twice.
The rifle went off, discharging a round into the ceiling.

senses.head: To officially let a patient leave the hospital
examples: They usually discharge you the next morning.
She was discharged after two nights.
He is being discharged this afternoon.

senses.head: To dismiss someone from a job or from military service
examples: He was discharged from the Army after four years.
A company may discharge an employee for theft.
Having been dishonorably discharged, he had trouble finding work.

senses.head: To send out liquid, gas, or waste
examples: The plant discharges wastewater into the river.
The factory discharged chemicals for years before anyone noticed.
Pipes along the roof were discharging steam into the cold air.

senses.head: To fire a gun
examples: It is illegal to discharge a firearm inside city limits.
The officer discharged his weapon twice.
The rifle went off, discharging a round into the ceiling.

entries.русский: выписывать (из больницы); увольнять, уволить; демобилизовать; сбрасывать, выбрасывать (отходы); выделять; стрелять, произвести выстрел
entries.contrast: The verb stresses the second syllable, dis-CHAHRJ; the noun a discharge stresses the first, DIS-chahrj.

entries.meaning: Ease has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Ice will ease the swelling.
The medication eased the pain within an hour.
His breathing is easing now.
He eased the car into the garage.
Ease the board into the slot; don't force it.
She was easing herself out of the chair when the phone rang.

senses.head: To make pain or a problem less severe, or to become less severe
examples: Ice will ease the swelling.
The medication eased the pain within an hour.
His breathing is easing now.

senses.head: To move something, or yourself, slowly and carefully into place
examples: He eased the car into the garage.
Ease the board into the slot; don't force it.
She was easing herself out of the chair when the phone rang.

entries.русский: облегчать, ослаблять (боль); осторожно двигать, подводить; медленно опускаться
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (ease the swelling), intransitive (the pain eased)
entries.phrasal verbs: ease into · ease off · ease out · ease up · ease up on

entries.meaning: Screen has 4 distinct senses.
examples: They screen everyone over fifty for colon cancer.
The hospital screened two thousand people last year.
She was screened and cleared.
The theater screens old westerns on Sunday nights.
They screened the documentary for the crew first.
The film has been screened at three festivals.
They screen every applicant before the interview.
Security screened all the bags at the door.
He was screening his calls all week.
Tall hedges screen the yard from the road.
A row of pines screened the house from the highway.
The patio is screened from the wind by a stone wall.

senses.head: To test a large group of healthy people in order to find a disease early
examples: They screen everyone over fifty for colon cancer.
The hospital screened two thousand people last year.
She was screened and cleared.

senses.head: To show a film or a program to an audience
examples: The theater screens old westerns on Sunday nights.
They screened the documentary for the crew first.
The film has been screened at three festivals.

senses.head: To check people or things in order to decide which ones to let through
examples: They screen every applicant before the interview.
Security screened all the bags at the door.
He was screening his calls all week.

senses.head: To hide or protect something from view, light, or wind
examples: Tall hedges screen the yard from the road.
A row of pines screened the house from the highway.
The patio is screened from the wind by a stone wall.

entries.русский: обследовать, проводить скрининг; показывать, показать (фильм); устраивать показ; проверять, проверить; отбирать (кандидатов); досматривать (багаж); заслонять, заслонить; закрывать (от вида, света); отгораживать

entries.meaning: Test has 3 distinct senses.
examples: They will test your blood for iron.
He tested positive on Monday.
She is being tested for allergies.
Engineers test every battery before it ships.
They tested the brakes on a closed track.
The software is still being tested.
Those two test my patience every single day.
The delay tested everyone's good humor.
He has been testing the limits of what we will allow.

senses.head: To check someone's blood, body, or ability with a medical procedure
examples: They will test your blood for iron.
He tested positive on Monday.
She is being tested for allergies.

senses.head: To use something in order to find out whether it works properly
examples: Engineers test every battery before it ships.
They tested the brakes on a closed track.
The software is still being tested.

senses.head: To put a strain on someone's patience or on the limits of something
examples: Those two test my patience every single day.
The delay tested everyone's good humor.
He has been testing the limits of what we will allow.

entries.русский: проверять, делать анализ; испытывать, испытать; проверять (работу), тестировать; испытывать (терпение), проверять на прочность
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (test her blood), intransitive (he tested positive)
entries.contrast: You test someone for something, and a person tests positive or tests negative.

entries.meaning: To rub and press someone's muscles to relieve pain or tension. ---
examples: Massage the cream into the muscle.
She massaged his neck for ten minutes.
He was massaging his calf where it cramped.
entries.contrast: Do not confuse massage /məˈsɑːʒ/ with message /ˈmɛsɪdʒ/, something you send.

entries.meaning: To wash your throat by holding liquid in it and breathing out.
examples: Gargle with warm salt water twice a day.
He gargled and spat into the sink.
She has been gargling since her throat started hurting.
